documents.title: Artificial Intelligence at NDSU: Goals, Guidance, and Research
documents.stance_why: The page says 'a framework for how AI is approached at NDSU, not a formal policy' and 'Instructors set course policies (including if AI use is allowed at all)'. The university sets no stance itself and hands the decision to instructors, so delegates.
documents.summary: This page summarizes NDSU's AI framework, which it says is 'not a formal policy', and links work-group documents for instructors, students and research. Instructors decide course AI use, AI contributions must be credited, and all AI use falls under existing integrity policies. It also notes research needs.

units.why: The page calls its content 'a framework for how AI is approached at NDSU, not a formal policy'. This states the status and scope of the guidance, so it informs; P56 (institution-level framework) fits.
units.anchor: a framework for how AI is approached at NDSU, not a formal policy

units.why: 'All use of AI falls under existing academic integrity, technology and other student/employee policies' binds everyone to existing rules. P77 fits better than P36 because it names no misconduct or penalty.
units.anchor: All use of AI falls under existing academic integrity, technology and other student/employee policies.

units.why: 'Instructors set course policies (including if AI use is allowed at all)' hands the decision to instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: Instructors set course policies (including if AI use is allowed at all)

units.why: 'all AI contributions must be credited' requires acknowledging AI use, so P24.
units.anchor: all AI contributions must be credited

units.why: 'should not replace critical thinking' says AI must not take over students' own thinking, so P32; 'should not' gives should-not.

units.why: 'Users are accountable for reliability, accuracy, and privacy (e.g., FERPA compliance)' makes users answerable for output accuracy and privacy. Accuracy is the lead so P31 rather than P50.

units.fit_note: Also makes users accountable for privacy (FERPA), which P31 does not capture.

units.anchor: Projects explore AI’s benefits, risks, and limitations.

units.anchor: Students develop prompt design, output evaluation, and AI literacy as professional competencies.

documents.title: AI in the Classroom: An NDSU Instructor Guide
documents.stance_why: The guide says 'Some instructors may encourage AI for brainstorming and revision, while others may prohibit its use altogether' and offers sample statements from allowed-with-credit to a ban on AI-written literature reviews. It sets no single rule and leaves the decision to instructors, so delegates.
documents.summary: Instructor guide with seven recommendations plus sample assignments and statements, mostly for writing. It urges clear expectations, transparency, AI skepticism, privacy care and AI literacy, and gives a suspected-misuse process that favors a conversation and a rewrite for first offenses. It says it was drafted with ChatGPT.
